content_voiceover: This slide details the molecular basis of chronic myeloid leukemia, focusing on the different BCR-ABL fusion isoforms that arise from the Philadelphia chromosome translocation. The reciprocal translocation between chromosome nine and chromosome twenty-two fuses the ABL1 gene from chromosome nine with the BCR gene on chromosome twenty-two, producing the derivative Philadelphia chromosome, twenty-two q minus. Depending on exactly where the breakpoint occurs within the BCR gene, three different breakpoint cluster regions produce three distinct fusion transcripts and corresponding protein isoforms. A breakpoint near the e1 locus, the minor breakpoint cluster region, generates the e1a2 transcript, which is translated into the p190 BCR-ABL protein. This p190 isoform accounts for only about one to two percent of CML cases but is the isoform most commonly seen in Philadelphia-chromosome-positive acute lymphoblastic leukemia, and when it does occur in CML it tends to be associated with monocytosis and a higher frequency of additional cytogenetic abnormalities. Breakpoints near the e13 or e14 loci, the major breakpoint cluster region, generate the e13a2 or e14a2 transcripts, producing the p210 BCR-ABL protein, which is by far the most common isoform and is the classic driver of typical chronic myeloid leukemia. A rarer breakpoint near the e19 locus, the micro breakpoint cluster region, generates the e19a2 transcript and the p230 BCR-ABL protein, an uncommon CML variant characterized by prominent chronic neutrophilia and a more indolent clinical course. Understanding which isoform is present matters for interpreting quantitative PCR monitoring, since the transcript type determines which primer sets are used to track molecular response during tyrosine kinase inhibitor therapy.
keypoints: Philadelphia chromosome: reciprocal translocation nine twenty-two fusing ABL1 with BCR
p210 (e13a2 or e14a2, major breakpoint region): the classic, most common CML isoform
p190 (e1a2, minor breakpoint region): more typical of Philadelphia-positive ALL, rare in CML
p230 (e19a2, micro breakpoint region): uncommon, indolent CML with prominent neutrophilia
keypoint_voiceover: Three isoforms to know. P210, from the major breakpoint region, is the workhorse transcript in typical CML. P190, from the minor breakpoint region, is more characteristic of Philadelphia-positive ALL, and when seen in CML brings monocytosis and extra cytogenetic changes. P230, from the micro breakpoint region, is a rare, indolent CML variant marked by chronic neutrophilia.
